note: Requirement summaries are plain-language paraphrases written for operational use. They are not legal text and not legal advice. Always read the cited source.

frameworks.name: EU AI Act
frameworks.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024

requirements.title: AI literacy
requirements.summary: Providers and deployers must ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

requirements.title: Prohibited AI practices
requirements.summary: Certain practices are banned outright, including manipulative techniques causing significant harm, exploitation of vulnerability, social scoring, untargeted facial scraping and workplace or education emotion inference.

requirements.title: High-risk classification
requirements.summary: A system is high-risk if it is a safety component of a regulated product or falls in an Annex III use case, unless a documented derogation assessment shows it does not pose a significant risk.

requirements.title: Risk management system
requirements.summary: A continuous, documented, iterative risk management system across the whole lifecycle: identify and evaluate known and foreseeable risks, adopt mitigations, and test that they work.

requirements.title: Data and data governance
requirements.summary: Training, validation and testing data must be governed: relevance, representativeness, bias examination and mitigation, and documented provenance and preparation.

requirements.title: Technical documentation
requirements.summary: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date, sufficient to demonstrate conformity to authorities.

requirements.title: Record-keeping and logging
requirements.summary: Automatic recording of events over the system's lifetime, enabling traceability of situations that may create risk or trigger substantial modification.

requirements.title: Transparency and information to deployers
requirements.summary: Instructions for use that state capabilities, limitations, accuracy metrics, foreseeable misuse, human oversight measures and expected lifetime.

requirements.title: Human oversight
requirements.summary: Design and build the system so that natural persons can effectively oversee it: understand its limits, interpret output, decide not to use it, and intervene or stop it.

requirements.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
requirements.summary: Appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle, with declared metrics and resilience to error, fault and adversarial attack including data poisoning.

requirements.title: Quality management system
requirements.summary: A documented QMS covering regulatory compliance strategy, design and testing procedures, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring and accountability.

requirements.title: Deployer obligations
requirements.summary: Use the system per instructions, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data relevance, monitor operation, keep logs, and inform workers before workplace deployment.

requirements.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment
requirements.summary: Certain deployers (public bodies, and private bodies in creditworthiness and life or health insurance pricing) must assess the impact on fundamental rights before first use.

requirements.title: Conformity assessment
requirements.summary: Undergo the applicable conformity assessment procedure before placing on the market, and again after substantial modification.

requirements.title: Registration in the EU database
requirements.summary: Register the high-risk system, or the derogation assessment, in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service.

requirements.title: Transparency for specific systems
requirements.summary: Tell people they are interacting with an AI system, mark synthetic content in machine-readable form, and disclose deep fakes and emotion or biometric categorisation.

requirements.title: General-purpose AI model obligations
requirements.summary: GPAI model providers must keep technical documentation, publish a training-content summary and operate a copyright policy.

requirements.title: Post-market monitoring
requirements.summary: A documented post-market monitoring plan that actively and systematically collects and analyses performance data over the system's lifetime.

requirements.title: Serious incident reporting
requirements.summary: Report serious incidents to the market surveillance authority of the Member State where the incident occurred, within the deadlines set by the Article.

requirements.title: Right to explanation of individual decisions
requirements.summary: Affected persons subject to an Annex III decision have the right to a clear and meaningful explanation of the role of the AI system in the decision procedure.

requirements.title: Principles of processing
requirements.summary: Lawfulness, fairness and transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality, and demonstrable accountability.

requirements.title: Lawful basis
requirements.summary: Each processing purpose needs an identified and documented lawful basis; a legitimate-interests basis needs a balancing assessment.

requirements.title: Special category data
requirements.summary: Processing of special category data, including biometric data for unique identification, is prohibited unless a specific condition applies.

requirements.title: Information to data subjects
requirements.summary: Tell people what is done with their data, including the existence of automated decision-making and the logic involved.

requirements.title: Right of access
requirements.summary: People can obtain confirmation, a copy of their data and meaningful information about automated decision-making applied to them.

requirements.title: Automated individual decision-making
requirements.summary: Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effect are restricted, and where permitted require human intervention, an explanation and the right to contest.

requirements.title: Data protection by design and by default
requirements.summary: Implement technical and organisational measures, including pseudonymisation and minimisation, at design time and by default.

requirements.title: Records of processing
requirements.summary: Maintain a record of processing activities, including purposes, categories, recipients, transfers and retention.

requirements.title: Security of processing
requirements.summary: Security appropriate to the risk, including confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, and regular testing of measures.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.summary: A DPIA is required where processing is likely to result in high risk, including systematic evaluation by automated means and large-scale special category processing.

requirements.title: International transfers
requirements.summary: Transfers outside the EEA need an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards or a derogation, plus a transfer risk assessment where relevant.

requirements.title: AI policy
requirements.summary: Top management establishes an AI policy appropriate to the organisation's purpose, communicated and available to interested parties.

requirements.title: AI system impact assessment
requirements.summary: Assess the potential consequences of AI systems for individuals, groups and society throughout the lifecycle.

requirements.title: Policies related to AI
requirements.summary: Documented AI policies, reviewed at planned intervals and aligned with other organisational policies.

requirements.title: Internal organisation
requirements.summary: Defined AI roles, responsibilities and reporting of concerns, including accountability for AI system outcomes.

requirements.title: Resources for AI systems
requirements.summary: Document the resources the AI system depends on: data, tooling, compute, human competence and model provenance.

requirements.title: Assessing impacts of AI systems
requirements.summary: A defined process for AI system impact assessment, including impacts on individuals and societies, and its documentation.

requirements.title: AI system lifecycle
requirements.summary: Objectives, requirements, design, verification, validation, deployment, operation and monitoring defined and documented for each system.

requirements.title: Data for AI systems
requirements.summary: Data provenance, quality, preparation and governance controls for data used in AI systems.

requirements.title: Information for interested parties
requirements.summary: Provide the information needed by users and affected parties, including intended use, limitations and how to raise concerns.

requirements.title: Use of AI systems
requirements.summary: Responsible use processes, including intended use boundaries and human oversight in operation.

requirements.title: Third-party and customer relationships
requirements.summary: Allocate and manage responsibilities across suppliers, model providers and customers in the AI value chain.

frameworks.name: NIST AI RMF
frameworks.citation: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (AI 100-1), January 2023

requirements.title: Legal and regulatory requirements understood
requirements.summary: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed and documented.

requirements.title: Roles and accountability
requirements.summary: Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication for AI risk are documented and clear to those involved.

requirements.title: Risk culture and critical thinking
requirements.summary: Organisational practices are in place that enable critical thinking and a safety-first mindset in AI design and deployment.

requirements.title: Third-party risk
requirements.summary: Policies address AI risks arising from third-party software, data and models.

requirements.title: Context established
requirements.summary: Intended purpose, setting, deployment context and expected users are understood and documented.

requirements.title: Scientific integrity and TEVV
requirements.summary: Test, evaluation, verification and validation are documented and mapped to the intended purpose.

requirements.title: Impacts on individuals and society
requirements.summary: Likelihood and magnitude of impacts on individuals, groups, communities and society are assessed.

requirements.title: Performance demonstrated
requirements.summary: AI system performance and assurance criteria are measured and demonstrated in conditions similar to deployment.

requirements.title: Security and resilience evaluated
requirements.summary: Security and resilience of the AI system are evaluated and documented, including adversarial testing.

requirements.title: Fairness and bias evaluated
requirements.summary: Fairness and bias are evaluated and results documented, including for subgroups.

requirements.title: Risk tracking mechanisms
requirements.summary: Approaches for tracking identified and emergent AI risks over time are in place.

requirements.title: Mechanisms to sustain value
requirements.summary: Mechanisms are in place to supersede, disengage or deactivate systems that demonstrate unintended behaviour.

requirements.title: Post-deployment monitoring plan
requirements.summary: Post-deployment monitoring plans are implemented, including capture and response to incidents and user feedback.

requirements.title: Incident communication
requirements.summary: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, affected communities and authorities.
